outlook.statement: Committed to investing in engineering capabilities, technology development, infrastructure and human capital to build solutions relevant to India's present requirements and prepared for future demands; contributing to India's defence capabilities and the vision of 'Make in India, Make for the World.'

The Company primarily focused on precision weapons, rocket launchers, surveillance communication equipment, Protective Vehicles, Defensive/ Deterrence Systems and Components. The Company has also Inauguration Bio-CNG & Hydrogen Fuel Plant, executed flag-off ceremony of Suryastra – 300 KM Universal Rocket Launching System and signed agreements for Space & Satellite Technologies.

Government's long-term vision under Space Vision 2047 includes ambitious goals such as establishing an indigenous space station, launching next-generation vehicles, and advancing deep space exploration missions.
Increase in defence spending by all major countries and the focus on infrastructure globally is acting as a tailwind for the Company's industrial business.
Domestic producers are given a preference in the defence sector which will provide new opportunities to the industry.
Diversification into aeronautics, space technologies, small arms, and defence electronics provides access to emerging high-growth verticals including UAVs, smart weapons, and satellite systems.

risks: As on the date of this report, the Company does not foresee any critical risk, which threatens its existence.
Challenges on inflation and supply chain persist globally
Central banks globally increasing rates to cool down inflation may adversely impact end customers demand
Rapid expansion and capital expenditure requirements place pressure on working capital, profitability and cash flow
Rising shortage of skilled labour, retaining workers remains a risk
Changing technology paradigms and dynamic customer needs
Disruption of movement of goods to customers due to global nature of business
Any shift of Government policies may have a meaningful impact on our business.
Global geopolitical developments and currency fluctuations may impact procurement priorities, export opportunities, and overall sector growth.
Several new companies are entering the market, and existing rivals in adjacent product categories are also increasing their offering.

Fluctuations in finished goods prices, raw material costs and their availability, fluctuations in global and domestic demand-supply dynamics, shifts in exchange rates, alterations in Government regulations and tax structures, as well as economic developments within India and the nations with which the Company maintains business ties.

The Company has established a robust framework for business risk evaluation and management, which is an ongoing process. The Board periodically reviews the identified risks and the measures implemented to mitigate them.

The Company has adequate risk assessment and minimization system in place including for commodities. The Company does not have material exposure of any commodity and accordingly, no hedging activities for the same are carried out.
Withdrawal: Actual withdrawals proving higher or lower than assumed withdrawals and change of withdrawals rates at subsequent valuations can impact the obligation.
Discount rate: Reduction in discount rate in subsequent valuations can increase the obligation.
Withdrawal rate risk: Actual withdrawals proving higher or lower than assumed can impact the obligation.
Discount rate risk: Reduction in discount rate can increase the obligation.
Mortality and disability risk: Actual deaths and disability cases proving lower or higher than assumed can impact the obligation.
Salary increase risk: Actual salary increases will increase the obligation; increase in salary increase rate assumption in future valuations will also increase the obligation.
Credit risk: Counterparty default on contractual obligations resulting in financial loss, primarily from trade receivables.
Liquidity risk: Risk of financial distress or high financing costs due to shortage of liquid funds.
Market risk: Foreign currency risk, interest rate risk, and commodity price risk.
litigation: There are no significant and material orders passed by the Regulators/Courts that would impact the going concern status of the Company and its future operations.
